text: {"bull":["Laurus Labs’ FY26 revenue rose 23% to ₹6,813 cr, driven by a 38% increase in small‑molecule CDMO sales to ₹1,896 cr.","The company’s operating profit grew from ₹1,055 cr in FY25 to ₹1,785 cr in FY26, while net profit surged from ₹358 cr to ₹890 cr, reflecting strong margin expansion.","Operating profit margin climbed from 24% in FY25 to 28% in FY26, and EBITDA margin increased from 26.1% to 26.8% in FY26, indicating improving operating leverage.","The company invested ₹394 cr in capex in Q1 FY27, supporting expansion of peptide and fermentation capacities, and maintained a debt‑to‑EBITDA of 1.28, close to the prior quarter’s 1.25.","The affordable medicines division generated ₹4,733 cr in FY26, an 18% YoY increase, with a 20% capacity expansion in oral solid formulation to 12 billion units.","R&D spend as a % of revenue rose to 5.8% in Q1 FY27, up 70% YoY, underscoring a commitment to high‑complexity technology development.","The company’s CDMO segment achieved a 69% YoY growth in Q1 FY27, with sales of ₹835 cr, highlighting strong demand for late‑stage clinical and commercial services.","The company’s gross margin of 62.7% in Q1 FY27, up 3.3 pp from the prior quarter, demonstrates efficient cost management across divisions."],"bear":["The company’s net profit margin fell from 6.4% in FY25 to 5.2% in FY26, indicating pressure on profitability despite revenue growth.","Operating profit margin only increased modestly from 24% in FY25 to 28% in FY26, suggesting limited margin expansion relative to revenue growth.","The debt‑to‑EBITDA ratio rose from 1.25 in Q4 FY26 to 1.28 in Q1 FY27, reflecting higher leverage due to capex spending.","R&D spend as a % of revenue increased to 5.8% in Q1 FY27, higher than the 4.1% in FY26, potentially impacting short‑term profitability.","The company’s gross margin in Q1 FY27 (62.7%) was only 3.3 pp above the prior quarter, indicating that margin improvement is incremental.","The affordable medicines division’s growth slowed to 18% in FY26 from 23% in FY25, suggesting a deceleration in that segment.","The company’s CDMO share of revenue increased to over 30% from 13% six years ago, but the ARV revenue share declined from 67% to 41%, indicating a shift that may affect cash flow stability.","The company’s net debt increased to ₹2,656 cr in Q1 FY27, up from ₹2,656 cr in Q4 FY26, showing a slight rise in leverage despite strong cash flows."]}
